description: We are Mechanical and Systems Engineering students at the University of San Carlos of Guatemala in Quetzaltenango. Our goal is to improve and acquire knowledge about the application of programming resources to solve specialized short-term problems, in order to create simulations and training programs for space missions.
summary:
A recreational simulator has been developed to foster knowledge about space exploration. In this interactive experience, users navigate various challenges, making decisions based on their own judgment as they lead a lunar mission in the Shackleton crater, with the goal of locating and collecting two elements essential for research back on Earth.
The project explores the subject of human survival on the Moon, highlighting, in particular, how the discovery and utilization of lunar resources are key to sustaining future habitats beyond our planet.
It serves as an important tool for introducing space science to young people fascinated by space-related topics. Designed to be both accessible and engaging, it ensures that users not only have fun but also gain an understanding of how humanity could live and thrive beyond Earth.
details:
What is it and how does it work?

Shackleton Camp is an educational space mission simulator, developed as part of the "Build a mission simulator for junior astronauts" challenge. In the game, the user takes on the role of an astronaut on the Moon, with the primary objective of exploring and collecting lunar regolith and ice to construct a human habitat. Throughout the mission, the player encounters real-world space hazards—such as solar storms or signal loss—and must make critical decisions to survive and achieve their goal. If an incorrect choice is made, the game provides a detailed scientific explanation of why that decision failed.

Benefits and intended impact

The project aims to spark an interest in science among children and young people worldwide by blending entertainment with genuine learning. It fosters critical thinking in decision-making and shares fascinating facts and fundamental concepts about how space works. Our long-term goal is to inspire new generations: a child who learns today how to protect a lunar base from radiation could, in the future, become the engineer or scientist who designs the first human habitat on Mars.

Tools and technology used

• Game engine: Unity

• Programming language: C#

• 3D modeling, assets, and textures: Blender

• Development operating systems: Windows and Linux

• Publicated on Github in carpet Realeses

Creativity and key factors

The project stands out by transforming errors into immediate learning opportunities through accessible scientific feedback, rather than simply displaying a "game over" screen. The "Mecasistemáticos" team prioritized scientific rigor tailored for a younger audience by creating an immersive, interactive environment with custom-designed graphical assets that visually and practically illustrate the real-world challenges of future lunar colonization.
